<description>
In a JSON-RPC batch, an element that is not an object gets an error reply with the id and version of the element before it.

`ExecuteHTTPRPC` parses every element of a batch into the same request object, and `parse()` throws on a non-object before it sets `id` and `m_json_version`. For `[{"jsonrpc":"2.0","method":"getblockcount","id":"X"}, 2]` the reply has two objects with `"id":"X"`, one with a result and one with an error. If the first element is a notification, the error is dropped. I give each element its own copy of the request, which holds only the HTTP fields, so the error is the one the first element of a batch already gets. The new case in `interface_rpc.py` fails on master and passes with this change.
</description>

Thanks for taking my suggestions.

EDIT: after further contemplation I think the change should be a followup:

I'm conflicted on one issue if this PR is complete or not, the behavior is different if bitcoind is started with `--rpcwhitelist` or not. Normally I would say the PR is incomplete, whitelist or not the response should be the same, but given this is already different on master I'm hesitant.

Batch | Without a whitelist | With a whitelist
-- | -- | --
Only valid elements | 200, array of replies | 200, array of replies
Contains "not an object" | 200, array, error only for that element | 400, one error object, nothing runs
Contains an object without method | 200, array, "Missing method" for that element | 500, one error object, nothing runs

This _can_ also be (partially) correct, if something from the batch cannot be checked by the whitelist -> fail everything. Given the [batch](https://www.jsonrpc.org/specification#batch) spec I would say we have to treat every call on it's own and failing everything for one failed call is not the correct response.

The 500 is in any case not correct
